description.en: Much of [Shimon] Ben Zoma's career paralleled that of his namesake, Shimon ben Azzai. He too studied under R. Yehoshua before becoming one of R. Akiva's greatest students. He too was overwhelmed when "entering the orchard."
description.he: פעילותו של שמעון בן זומא מקבילה לרוב לזו של שמעון בן עזאי, שעל שמו נקרא. גם הוא למד עם רבי יהושע לפני שהיה לאחד מגדולי התלמידים של רבי עקיבא, וגם הוא נפגע כאשר "נכנס לפרדס".

image_caption.en: "He Cast a Look and Went Mad", Maurycy Minkowski 1910. The caption at the bottom is a quote from the Talmud Chagigah 14b:  "glimpsed and was harmed". Gift of Mrs. Rose Mintz, The Jewish Museum, New York.
image_caption.he: "הוא הביט ונטרפה דעתו", מאוריצי מינקובסקי, 1910. הכיתוב בתחתית הוא ציטוט מהתלמוד, חגיגה יד ב: "הציץ ונפגע". מתנת גברת רוז מינץ, המוזיאון היהודי, ניו יורק.

en.title: Contemplating Creation
en.prompt: Ben Zoma is known for his questionable mystical speculation. The Tosefta, a late 2nd-century compilation of Jewish oral law, recounts a story of a revealing encounter Ben Zoma had with the elder sage Rabbi Joshua.
en.ai_prompt: Ben Zoma's exploration of divine Creation and cosmic dimensions led him to a unique interpretation of the proximity between earthly and heavenly realms, ultimately causing his divergence from mainstream Jewish thought. The Tosefta, a late 2nd-century compilation of Jewish oral law, highlights the tension between mystical speculation and mainstream rabbinic thought, reflecting concerns about the dangers of delving too deeply into esoteric matters.

en.title: The Perils of the Pardes
en.prompt: The experience of 'entering the orchard' (pardes) led to different outcomes for each of four sages, with Ben Zoma tragically going mad. Ein Yaakov, a collection of Talmudic stories and teachings, recounts the story of the 'four who entered the pardes,' which has been interpreted to refer to esoteric knowledge and mystical experience.

en.title: Remembering the Exodus Daily
en.prompt: The daily and nightly remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt is a fundamental aspect of Jewish life, as derived from the Torah and specifically inferred by Ben Zoma. Rabbi Eliezer Melamed’s contemporary work, Peninei Halakhah, explains how this commandment is fulfilled through the recitation of the third paragraph of Shema each morning and evening.

en.title: Legacy of Ben Zoma
en.prompt: Ben Zoma's wisdom was so revered that his death marked the end of an era of great preaching. Gershom Bader's early 20th-century biography of Shimon ben Zoma highlights his esteemed education, his role as a preacher, and the significant impact of his death on Jewish preaching.
